verdicts.gap_id: A1 — one-shot latch descriptor discarded at annotate_capability_one_shot
verdicts.reason: The persistence half survives every attack I could mount. Re-measured independently: 39 one_shot conditions (23 protocol-1 / 16 NULL), key set exactly {description,kind,latch_state,latch_target,latch_value} on 39/39, 0 of 1799 effective_functions mention any dropped strength field, latch_value distribution 1×31 / 2×4 / 3×3 / 11473216×1. Stop-discarding-the-transcript invents nothing and adds no RPC. Two over-claims survive in the *witness* the gap proposes. (1) STRENGTH ORDERING: `latch_basis` is proposed with an explicit order sentinel > version_ge > value_gt_zero ≈ guard, but sentinel and value_gt_zero fired on ZERO rows and guard on 6 (0 at protocol-1). A ranking over branches that never executed cannot be validated on this corpus, and B14 bars calibrating it on the 6; publish the four bases as distinct three-state labels that GATE and CITE, and publish the ordering — if any — as a named model choice with its version, never as a measured reliability. (2) PERMANENCE: I verified latch_target='db_linked_proxy' on 39/39 rows, i.e. every latched contract is read through a proxy. `latch_state='consumed'` therefore proves only that the latch was consumed in the implementation live at probe_block; a `reinitializer(n+1)` shipped by the upgrade authority re-opens the initializer. The fix adds probe_block (good) but leaves `isInertOneShot` → protection 0.95 (site/src/protocolScore.js:239) reading `consumed` as permanent inertness, which is a mutable now-fact published as an invariant plus an inv.10 violation (no counterfactual naming who can re-open it). Also note the fix's own admission must be enforced: `expected_version` comes from a modifier NAME set (INITIALIZER_MODIFIERS), so it is only publishable carrying expected_version_basis, never as compiler-forced.
verdicts.provable_core: Persist, on the next resolution pass only, the transcript facts the producer already holds — standard, slot, byte_offset, size_bytes, value_type, raw_word, probe_block, guard {operator,constant}, expected_version + expected_version_basis — with keys ABSENT (never null, never defaulted) where the producer had nothing, and `latch_basis` published as a four-valued discriminator plus not_determined. Consumer obligations: an absent latch_witness reads as the weakest branch; the 6 no-descriptor rows (protocol-1 ef 479, 480, 1456, 2745) publish latch_basis and probe_block as not_determined; and the inertness credit is published as "consumed at block <probe_block>; re-openable by the upgrade authority of <proxy>" because latch_target='db_linked_proxy' on 39/39 — not as a static protection constant. No strength ORDERING is published as a measured fact.

verdicts.gap_id: A2 — exact-empty caller sets lose last_indexed_block / empty_reason; predicate_evaluator.py:783's provenance-less exact-empty
verdicts.reason: Measurements reproduce to the row: 85 exact-empty enumerable finite_sets (52 protocol-1 / 33 NULL), empty_reason on 1 of 52, last_indexed_block on 0 of 52, 4 zero-trace empties corpus-wide (2 protocol-1), and 261 protocol-1 solmate finite_sets with last_indexed_block absent ANYWHERE in the tree (not just at top level). The combinator fix's fail-closed rule (propagate only when EVERY finite operand carries a height; empty_reason only on inherited emptiness) is stricter than the consumer's own MIN and is sound. Three over-claims. (1) I read the code the fix depends on: predicate_evaluator.py's live read is `eth_call [..., hex(block) if isinstance(block, int) else "latest"]`. So `outer.block` is frequently None and the read genuinely goes to "latest" (FIELDS.md §4 records exactly that for controller reads). `observed_at_block` may be emitted ONLY when block is an int; on the "latest" path it must publish not_determined and the earned-negative credit must be withheld, or the fix stamps a bounded-in-time claim onto an unbounded read. (2) The consumer gate (iv) lets a row keep the 0.95 credit on the strength of `empty_reason` presence — and I broke that on the exact row the gap names as keeping it: ef 192 PriceProvider.claimGovernance carries `empty_reason='empty_by_design'`, no trace, no selector, no block, and `empty_by_design` is a DEFAULT ARGUMENT VALUE in `_live_resolve_authority_slot(..., zero_empty_reason: EmptyReason | None = "empty_by_design")`. A default standing in for a witness is an auto-refute; ef 192 must lose the credit alongside ef 1613/797/1151 until its producing path is identified. (3) For NON-empty member sets, MIN over operands at different heights is not an exactness as-of: intersect(A@b1, B@b2) is neither a superset nor a subset of the true set at MIN when B changed in (b1,b2]. MIN is sound for the exact-EMPTY case (published ⊇ true@MIN, so empty ⇒ empty at MIN) and for equal-height operands (all 80 cursors are at 25641245 today), and it is sound as a STALENESS floor, which is all capability_currency uses it for. It must not be published as "this set was exact at block MIN".
verdicts.provable_core: (a) Stop the four strip sites (capabilities.py:507/:527/:543 and both negate arms :416/:428) dropping last_indexed_block and empty_reason, propagating only when every finite operand carries one, and empty_reason only on inherited emptiness. (b) Publish the height with the semantics the consumer already documents — a fold-coverage/staleness floor, licensing capability_currency; for an exact-EMPTY result it additionally licenses "empty at block MIN"; for a non-empty exact set at heterogeneous heights publish `exact_as_of: not_determined`. (c) `_live_authority_result` gains block + selector + contract trace and `empty_reason='owner_read_zero'`, with observed_at_block emitted only when the call was pinned (not_determined on the "latest" path). (d) The burn branch never shares the zero shape. (e) The consumer gate requires trace[0].step AND an observation block AND a non-defaulted empty_reason — which withdraws the credit from ef 192 as well as ef 1613 (protocol-1), ef 797, ef 1151.

verdicts.gap_id: A3 — accessor-convention basis published only inside details->'trace'[*].basis
verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly: a single group of 33 rows, basis='internal_accessor_convention', membership_quality='exact', confidence='enumerable', resolved_type='safe', collapsing to 2 distinct principals across 3 runtime addresses (0xa000244b via 6 CumulativeMerkleDrop rows; 0xf46d3734 via 27 LRTSquared/PriceProvider rows); slot_name_keyword = 0 rows. Hoisting the basis to a top-level `details.authority_basis` is pure re-publication of a computed fact and is right; the refusal of the slot-scan differential (unrunnable on 2 of 3 addresses, non-identifying on the third) is the correct call and I could not improve on it. The over-claim is the proposed STRENGTH ORDER `abi_auto_getter > standard_namespaced_accessor > deunderscore_convention`. `abi_auto_getter` is genuinely stronger (solc mints the getter from the declaration — no name is consulted). But the other two are both accessor-NAME matches, and nothing measured here establishes that an ERC-7201-anchored accessor-name match is more reliable evidence *that the accessor returns the authority* than the 3-name convention: the gap's own residual `accessor_slot_agreement: not_determined` applies identically to both arms, and its own could-not-verify says the 6 CumulativeMerkleDrop rows' arm assignment rests on a docstring, not on a readable blob (those rows are also in the A1 no-descriptor set). Publishing a rank promotes 6 rows on unverified arm attribution.
verdicts.provable_core: Publish `details.authority_basis` at top level beside membership_quality/confidence, split into the labels the producer can distinguish at the write point (abi_auto_getter / standard_namespaced_accessor / deunderscore_convention / slot_name_keyword), absent = not_determined = weakest. Rank ONLY abi_auto_getter above the two name-matched arms; leave those two mutually UNORDERED (a shared 'accessor_name_matched' tier) with `accessor_slot_agreement: not_determined` on both, and cite the co-witness that does exist (live_getter_resolution on 33/33). Any finer ordering is a model choice published with its version, and per B14 (2 principals / 3 addresses) it may only gate, cite or three-state — never weight.

verdicts.gap_id: B1 — contract_balances has no block_number; destructive per-contract DELETE + re-insert
verdicts.reason: Re-measured: 721 protocol-1 rows / 26 distinct fetched_at / span 01:40:25.469544 / 60 entities, and the column list is exactly (id, contract_id, token_address, token_name, token_symbol, decimals, raw_balance, usd_value, price_usd, fetched_at) — no block_number, no observed_address. `observed_address` capture is unimpeachable (a local variable at both write points). The block, published ONLY on the pinned-multicall path with NULL = not_determined, is likewise honest, and the refusal to stamp an eth_blockNumber beside an Etherscan answer is the right call. Two problems. (1) PRICE LAUNDERING: the fix stamps block_number on a row that also carries price_usd and usd_value, while the gap itself establishes price has no height and diverges up to 20.97% for the same asset within a single recorded instant. A consumer reading that row reads a USD figure as-of a block that only the quantity was observed at. The row must carry a separate price provenance (`price_observed_at: not_determined`), and usd_value must not inherit the quantity's block. (2) NULL-BLOCK DUPLICATION: the proposed unique key (contract_id, observed_address, token_address, block_number) does not constrain the Etherscan path at all (NULLs are distinct in a Postgres unique index), so insert-only growth there is unbounded and the `latest` view becomes the only safe read — every existing reader (services/effects/selection.py, company_overview, workers/policy_worker.py, the three prototype scorers) must be migrated in the same commit or a consumer sums across heights. The gap's own could-not-verify admits it did not audit those readers for a one-row-per-(contract,asset) assumption.
verdicts.provable_core: (a) `observed_address` captured verbatim at both write points — provable today, no new evidence. (b) `asset_set_completeness ∈ {at_page_cap, not_determined}` from the raw page length — no 'complete' value exists. (c) `block_number` populated only on the pinned Multicall3 path, NULL = not_determined permanently for all 1,617 existing rows, and scoped to raw_balance ONLY: price_usd/usd_value carry their own `price_observed_at: not_determined` and are never presented as priced-at-block. (d) Insert-only plus a `latest` view, landed together with the migration of every identified reader; the two unrepairable entity rows (contracts.id 544 AuctionManager, 563 StakingManager) publish observed_address and have their USD withdrawn as an M7/16a defect rather than re-keyed by guesswork.

verdicts.gap_id: B2 — absent native row conflates proven-zero with fetch-failure
verdicts.reason: The code fact reproduces (41 of 60 protocol-1 entities have no native row; 19 native / 702 ERC-20 / 721 total) and the three-state discriminator is exactly right in principle: a pinned eth_getBalance returning 0x0 IS a proven zero, an exception IS a proven failure, and both must stop sharing an absence. But the DELIVERY MECHANISM trips the auto-refute on the brief's list — 'always insert a balance row changing absent-row semantics for consumers that currently read absence as not_determined'. I checked the consumer rather than assuming: services/effects/selection.py:422-448 `_asset_holdings_by_deployment` joins ContractBalance with NO positive-balance filter and keys (holder, asset) with `asset = _addr(token_address) or NATIVE_ASSET_LOG_EMITTER`, so a row's mere EXISTENCE is consumed as 'this deployment holds this asset'. Inserting 41 native rows with raw_balance=0 (and usd_value NULL) publishes 41 holdings that do not exist, and it mutates the protocol-wide `value_holders` set that `_add_reach` gates on — the same set whose emptiness/non-emptiness decides B4's reach branches on the 43 proven flow.out rows (43 confirmed by my recount, 87 flow.out claims / 43 with `observed`). An added unpriced pair lands in the observed_reach_unvalued_pairs branch, so a row currently publishing a measured `observed_reach_value_usd` can flip to reach_determined=false, and vice versa. B2's 'flips_existing_rows: None numerically' is therefore wrong.
verdicts.provable_core: Keep the three states — native_status ∈ {proven_zero (pinned path only), proven_nonzero, fetch_failed} and asset_set_status ∈ {returned_assets, returned_empty, fetch_failed, at_page_cap} — and add the missing record_degraded(phase='balance_fetch') to the tvl.py native path so both writers leave the same trace. But do NOT deliver it by inserting rows into `contract_balances` while that table's row existence is a holdings witness. Either (i) put the discriminator in a separate fetch-provenance plane keyed (contract, observed_address, asset, block) whose rows are explicitly NOT holdings, or (ii) change `_asset_holdings_by_deployment` and `_token_holdings_by_contract` in the SAME commit to require a positive witnessed balance, and re-measure the 43 reach rows before and after. The damage population for the conflation itself is 0 rows (0 of 41 nonzero at time-aligned pinned blocks), so this is a representation fix and must be argued from the code contract, never used to calibrate anything (B14).

verdicts.gap_id: B3 — fork verdicts span 51 distinct blocks in one run
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: 274 effect_verdicts, 0 with witness.block_number, witness carrying exactly 20 keys and no block key (FIELDS.md §7's 'effect_verdicts.witness.block_number 304/304' is wrong on both location and denominator, as the lane says). Publishing the height is pure re-publication and passing --fork-block-number is a name-free plumbing change; both survive. Two hazards the proposal creates. (1) SEQUENCING: for the 78 tier-2 rows the preflight block is provably NOT the fork height, so shipping (a) without (b) stamps a fabricated observation height onto 78 rows including all four proven freeze verdicts (ids 137/149/173/219). The lane states this in honest_publication but its proposed_witness reads 'the preflight pin for tier 1' — the implementer must be told that for tier 2 the field is emitted only where --fork-block-number was actually passed, and never as 0 (today block=0 is the failure sentinel and would read as genesis). (2) IDENTITY: adding the block to uq_effect_verdicts_identity (chain_id, contract_address, selector, effect_class) converts an upsert into an append, so multiple verdict rows per key exist with no selection rule and a consumer can publish a verdict observed at an older height as the current fact. It also silently contradicts B5's cost argument, which relies on the same unique key upserting in place.
verdicts.provable_core: (b) Pass --fork-block-number str(ctx.block) at services/effects/anvil.py:676, then (a) publish witness.block_number + witness.block_source ∈ {invocation_pin, job_pin, run_pin} — tier 1 from the preflight pin, tier 2 only where the fork was actually pinned. All 274 existing verdicts, and the 78 tier-2 rows in particular, publish height not_determined; nothing is back-filled. If the block enters the verdict identity, ship a 'latest height wins' selection rule with it and reconcile with B5's in-place-upsert assumption; a per-run pin is a separate schema decision (jobs has no run/batch column) and delivers intra-run coherence, not replayability.

verdicts.gap_id: B4 — observed_reach_floor_usd and its siblings produced on 0 rows
verdicts.reason: I attacked this looking for a minted witness and there is none — this is the only lane that refuses to fix anything, and it is right. Recounted every `observed` key over protocol-1 claims: exactly 21 keys are populated (destination_shape/observed_reach_assets/observed_reach_holders/reach_determined/shape_proved_by 43, reach_tvl_check 41, input_seeded 39, observed_reach_value_usd 38, unvalued ×5, priced ×3, the four pause keys ×4, contract_balance_seeded 2) and observed_reach_floor_usd, observed_reach_rejected_usd, protocol_tvl_usd and reach_indeterminate are absent entirely; 87 flow.out claims with 43 carrying `observed`, so 44 have none. The reclassification from 'implemented but 0 rows' to 'live branch, unmet data precondition' is a documentation correction, the proposal explicitly mints no field, and the honest publication (reach = not_determined on the 44 static-only rows; the 3 priced rows as directional lower bounds $908,232.04 / $1,708,327.33 / $41,517.24) is what inv.16's floor clause requires. One residual to state rather than a weakening: the reachability test pins `observed_reach_floor_usd: 0.0`, and in production that 0.0 is sourced from acting_balance_usd, i.e. from B1/B2's blockless and absence-conflated balance plane — so a 0.0 floor must be consumed as 'no proven bound' beside reach_indeterminate=true, never as a measured zero. Because the branch has zero realized rows, that is a contract statement, not a measured defect (B14).

verdicts.gap_id: B5 — auto_expiry / duration_bound_seconds populated on zero; duration_bound_source not_determined 4/4
verdicts.reason: The measurements hold — 4 rows (effect_verdicts 137/149/173/219, all freeze_pause/proven/tier2/selector 0x7e3db158), auto_expiry NULL and duration_bound_seconds NULL and duration_bound_source='not_determined' on 4/4 — and I re-read the four pauseUntilDuration values at pinned block 25643300 byte-exactly (172800 / 86400 / 28800 / 28800; MAX_PAUSE_DURATION 2592000, MIN 28800 on 4/4), plus the negative control the lane admits it never ran: 0xdeadbeef / 0x1234abcd / 0xffffffff all revert bare on all four, so the getters are not a catch-all. But the PROPOSED WITNESS converts a not_determined into a severity-REDUCING proven positive on $4.05B, and two chain facts break it. (1) The window is MUTABLE and its setter exists. `pauseUntil()` is NULLARY (abi_signature 'pauseUntil()' on all 10 rows carrying selector 0x7e3db158), so the duration comes from storage; and at 25643300 `setPauseUntilDuration(uint256)` DISPATCHES on all four contracts — it reverts with custom-error data 0xadb09821 (a guard rejection) while `setPauseUntilDuration(uint32)` and `totallyBogusFn(uint256)` revert with no data at all, the same discrimination that distinguishes the known-real pauseUntil() (0xcae1d956) and unpauseUntil() (0x204a4197). So a fork-observed recovery at rung R measures only the duration configured at the fork block, which the setter's holder can raise to 2,592,000s. (2) RE-PAUSE. Nothing observed in the ladder prevents re-invoking pauseUntil() the instant the latch expires, so the EFFECTIVE freeze is unbounded whatever any per-call ceiling says — and that is not hypothetical: B0b/R1 of this very register concludes that 4 keys inside the 'protective' 4/7 'can freeze and hold the freeze indefinitely' on exactly these contracts (WeETH $3,502,642,106, EETH, LiquidityPool $77,255,816, EtherFiRestaker $467,568,890). Publishing auto_expiry=True / duration_bound_source='fork_observed_recovery' would therefore contradict the register's own headline finding, lower severity on a 4-row population B14 bars calibrating on, and fire a lowering field on something other than its proven-present state (inv.16d). Variant (a), the declared-ceiling read, fails identically: it bounds one call, not the freeze. Provable residue, publishable as a LABEL with zero severity effect: 'on a fork at block B, with pauseUntilDuration = D read at B, one pauseUntil() call's effect ended after R seconds of warp; the duration is settable (setPauseUntilDuration exists at B) and re-pause was not excluded'. B0b/R12's rule stands unchanged — duration contributes zero to severity in either direction — and the inspector's current 'indefinite latch (no self-recovery bound)' string must still become 'window not determined', which needs no new witness.

verdicts.gap_id: C1 — Safe modules and guard never probed
verdicts.reason: The lane's refutation of B0b/R1's closing caveat is CONFIRMED and is the most valuable finding in Group C. Safe populations reproduce (function_principals 19 distinct, control_graph_nodes 18, protocol-1-scoped 11, monitored_contracts 11 — no plane yields 9), and I independently walked the module linked list on 0x21f73d42eb58ba49ddb685dc29d3bf5c0f0373ca at pinned 25643300: slot keccak256(abi.encode(0x1,uint256(1))) = 0xcc69885f… holds 0x…2e1b5a40edc922bce489668b11749b8eabd67f6b, the next link terminates at the sentinel 0x1, getModulesPaginated(sentinel,10) returns a 1-element array, guard slot 0x4a204f62… is zero, VERSION() = '1.1.1', getThreshold() = 4, singleton (slot 0) = 0x34cfac646f301356faa8b21e94227e3583fe3f5f, module codelen 5451 bytes. So k/n IS an upper bound on 1 of 19 Safes and FIELDS.md:84 is refuted. The over-claim is in the proposed classifier witness: because the batched calldata builders cannot pass arguments, the fix is TWO eth_getStorageAt reads, which give the linked-list HEAD only — yet the proposal publishes `modules` as an array and its test (2) asserts modules == ['0x2e1b…'] from that head word. A Safe with two modules would publish a one-element list as if enumerated. The completeness of this particular list came from a walk (my 2 extra reads) or from the argument-bearing eth_call, neither of which the fix performs.
verdicts.provable_core: From the two-storage-read classifier publish `modules_head` (the raw word) and derive only the PROVEN-EMPTY determination: head == sentinel ⇒ `module_set: []` with basis 'storage_linked_list_terminated' at probe_block; head != sentinel ⇒ `module_set: not_determined` plus `protection_is_upper_bound: true` and the head address cited. Publish an enumerated `modules` array only where the list was actually walked to the sentinel (k extra reads) or the paginated eth_call returned with next == sentinel. Keep the guard three-state as proposed (proven_address / proven_zero for 1.3.0+1.4.1 / feature_absent for 1.1.1 / not_determined), keep the version and probe_block mandatory, and keep 'no module has ever been enabled' as not_determined absent a warm EnabledModule cursor from creation. Populations 1 (module-bearing) and 4 (its reach, all protocol_id IS NULL) may not calibrate anything.

verdicts.reason: Verified to the row and I could not find a minted witness in it. contracts.id=11 'Operating Timelock' 0xcd425f44758a08baab3c4908f3e3de5776e45d7a has job_id NULL, source_verified NULL, compiler_version NULL and ZERO effective_functions, while its twins id=12 (0x9f26d4c9, v0.8.13) and id=472 (0x70a64840, v0.8.21) have 12 each; its reach is 53 function_principals rows across 16 contracts. On the value figure my first aggregation disagreed and I was wrong, not the lane: sum-all-rows, sum-of-MAX-per-(contract,token) and MAX-per-(holder,asset) all return $4,056,989,156.20 exactly. The fix publishes nothing — it runs one analysis job whose expected output shape is a compiler-derived fact known in advance — and the interim publication is the correct three-state (`proposer_set: not_determined`, kind timelock_proposer_unresolved), with an explicit refusal to substitute the twins' role grants. Three conditions I attacked and found already stated or harmless: the perimeter cause is a budget (analyze_limit=2, rank 0.3836 at positions 42-57), not a bug, so the fix is one job and not a threshold change; the post-run proposer set is an event fold needing its own cursor coverage and block; and the 2-day delay may not be credited as a mitigation merely by existing (B0b/R12). Two things must ride along: the delay=172800 that 53 rows already publish is a duck-typed nullary read and needs the PR#161 negative control (a nonsense selector must revert) before it is cited as a proven ordinal, and the offline producer test must fail loudly rather than skip if solc 0.8.25 is unprovisioned (the label-corpus gate skips silently on SolcNotInstalled).

verdicts.gap_id: C3 — ManagerWithMerkleVerification absent from contracts (10 addresses)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly: 10 distinct `manage` principals / 20 rows / 0 present in `contracts`, and the perimeter mechanism is confirmed at the population level — control_graph_nodes with details->>'source'='semantic_capability:role_grant' and node_type='contract' number 32 addresses of which 19 have no job (plus 7 principal-typed, all jobless). The fix is a missing `_queue_discovered_contracts` call after the policy stage's replace_control_graph_rows, with every needed local in scope; it publishes no fact by itself. I attacked the witness rather than the plumbing: the load-bearing facts are the pinned `vault()` back-link (10/10) and the finite-set membership fold, NOT the control_graph_nodes.label string 'ManagerWithMerkleVerification' — the lane says so explicitly and refuses the name. The residual it keeps three-state is the right one: `manageRoot(strategist)` is a hash, so the strategist's admissible call set stays not_determined even after the managers are analysed, and 'the manager is analysed' must never become 'the manage capability is bounded'. Conditions: the recursive-fanout budget must LOG its cut (a silently dropped candidate is the C2 defect reappearing), which also means test (7)'s population invariant `… no-job count == 0` must be written as 'zero unlogged omissions', not 'zero omissions', or a legitimate budget cut reddens the gate; and the 30 manager-attributable `contract_gated_unknown_path` warnings that resolve may move in either polarity, so the current zero contribution stays correct until they do.

verdicts.gap_id: C4 — upgrade sender / who authorised an upgrade
verdicts.reason: Schema and counts reproduce absolutely: upgrade_events columns are exactly (id, contract_id, proxy_address, old_impl, new_impl, block_number, timestamp, tx_hash, source) with no sender/from/executor anywhere in the schema, 120 protocol-1 events / 68 distinct tx / 24 proxies, 191 table-wide. The strongest parts are unbreakable: `authorising_eoa: not_determined` on every Safe/timelock-mediated tx (6 relayers measured for one Safe), `governance_action_id = tx_hash` (the only structural fix for the 19× fanout), and `is_deployment` from receipt.to == null AND receipt.contractAddress == proxy_address. The over-claim is `eoa_one_hop`, where the fix says tx.from 'is the authoriser as a matter of EVM semantics'. receipt.to == proxy proves tx.from was msg.sender in the TOP-LEVEL frame; it does not prove tx.from was msg.sender at the upgrade site (a self-call, a multicall/batch entry point, or an ERC-2771/signature-guarded upgrade path all break it), and it does not prove the upgrade's guard reads msg.sender at all — that is an AST claim the receipt fold cannot make. Population 4, so B14 bars generalising from it. Second, smaller point: `safe_direct`/`timelock_routed` rest partly on the ABSENCE of the other marker in the receipt; that is admissible only because a receipt's log set is complete for its transaction by construction, so that completeness property must be published as the basis rather than assumed, and the 8 intermediary-mediated txs stay not_determined as proposed.
verdicts.provable_core: Publish per distinct tx_hash: `is_deployment` (airtight), `governance_action_id = tx_hash`, `executor_kind ∈ {timelock_routed, safe_direct, not_determined}` gated on the emitter being INDEPENDENTLY classified (an unclassified ExecutionSuccess emitter ⇒ not_determined), `receipt_log_set_complete_for_tx: true` as the stated basis for the marker-absence reasoning, and `authorising_eoa: not_determined` on ALL rows including the 4 one-hop ones. Where receipt.to == proxy, publish the narrower proven fact `top_level_msg_sender: <tx.from>` and NOT `authoriser`. Keep `timelock_is_decoy: not_determined` on all 24 proxies (0-after-first-timelock is an absence of observed bypass) and publish only the positive `direct_upgrade_witnessed_at_block: B`. The deployment reclassification (18 of 120) legitimately rewrites the published counts downward (EtherFiNodesManager 18→17, LiquidityPool 17→16, 0x2b90103c 1→0) and the day-figure '11 proxies on 2026-07-14' to 19.

verdicts.gap_id: D1 — restaking / position value on EtherFiNode
verdicts.reason: I re-ran the pinned reads and they reproduce byte-exactly at block 25643300: podOwnerDepositShares(0x53e1eb2f…) = 0x1a055690d9db80000 = 30e18, getPod = 0xb274d6b6…, activeValidatorCount = 3, withdrawableRestakedExecutionLayerGwei = 0, node and pod native balances 0, getWithdrawableShares([beaconChainETH]) also 30e18, and negative controls (0xdeadbeef) revert on both EigenPodManager and the pod. The provenance half (eigenpod, active_validator_count, last_checkpoint_timestamp, consensus_layer_residual: not_determined as a string never 0) is honest and I could not break it. The FLOOR is where it over-claims, on two counts. (1) ENTITY (inv.16a). The fix's flips section raises the published reach of effective_functions id 1184 (EtherFiNode 0x556db8c6…) and id 2038 from floored to a directional lower bound — but 0x556db8c6 is the BEACON IMPLEMENTATION, whose own getEigenPod() is 0x0, and the lane itself proved that. Attaching any node's position to that row attributes a balance sheet to the wrong entity, and attaching it to a capability requires a destination witness that forwardExternalCall can reach the EigenLayer withdrawal path — the row's destination_constraint.state is 'not_determined'. That is precisely inv.16a's sweepETH error (5,188× over-valuation) in a new place. (2) MAGNITUDE. 3 active validators against 30e18 shares means the consensus-layer residual is on the order of 66 ETH, i.e. the proposed 'floor' is roughly a third of the plausible position — publishable as a floor only with its direction and never as a value at stake, and never summed with spot balances in the same column.
verdicts.provable_core: Publish, per ENUMERATED node instance (not per contracts row, and never on the beacon implementation), a position record at a recorded block: {eigenpod, position_shares_wei with basis 'eigenlayer_withdrawable_shares' cross-read via getWithdrawableShares, active_validator_count, last_checkpoint_timestamp, consensus_layer_residual: 'not_determined'}, with getEigenPod()==0x0 ⇒ {position_shares_wei: 0, basis: 'no_eigenpod_proven'} as a distinct proven-zero, and a failed read ⇒ null ⇒ not_determined (never 0). Do NOT consume it as reach for ef 1184/2038 until a destination witness proves the capability reaches the withdrawal path; until then both rows stay reach = not_determined. If it is ever published as a floor it carries its direction ('>= $X') and its own basis column so it can never be summed with a spot balance. verdicts.gap_id: D2 — ERC-20 asset identity on static flows (witness.sink_ids carries a variable name only)
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: 217 sink_ids entries over protocol-1 claims, 0 matching an address regex. The structural descriptor is the right instrument and the parameter arm is the strongest part — `asset_identity = caller_named, param_index = n` is a positive compiler fact that DEMOTES pricing on 7 rows, which is direction-safe. The over-claim is the immutable arm. I checked the entity keying and every immutable row is an IMPLEMENTATION fronted by a proxy: ef 472 contract 454 → proxy 0x6db24ee6, ef 1532 contract 535 → 0x35fa1647, ef 1551/1565 contract 534 → 0x35e7d6fe, ef 1649 contract 551 → 0x3d320286, ef 2288 contract 613 (0xa6ca0607) → 0xcd5fe23c, ef 2568 contract 626 → 0xdadef1ff, and effective_functions.deployment_address confirms the runtime addresses (ef 2288 → 0xcd5fe23c). An `immutable` is inlined in the IMPLEMENTATION's bytecode, so `mutability: immutable` is not an invariant at the runtime address a consumer prices against — the upgrade authority changes it, and 0xcd5fe23c is one of the proxies the register records as repeatedly upgraded. Publishing 'immutable' as the strength gate for an asset identity therefore publishes an invariant the evidence does not support. (The mutable case, ef 2310's getTokenOut(), the lane already handles correctly as storage_setter, proven at a block, redirectable.)
verdicts.provable_core: Publish the receiver descriptor {binding ∈ {parameter, state_variable, local, not_determined}, param_index, mutability, visibility, auto_getter_selector} as an AST fact, and resolve `asset_address` by pinned eth_call only for binding=state_variable AND visibility=public AND a nullary auto-getter — but label the mutability `immutable_in_implementation` and pair every resolved address with `observed_at_block` plus `asset_identity_invariant: not_determined` (or 'redirectable_by_upgrade_authority') wherever deployment_address is a proxy, which is 7 of the 10 immutable rows. `caller_named` on the 7 parameter rows stands as-is and must FAIL FIELDS.md §3's token_identity precondition. The `local` bucket is 1 row and `constant` is 0 rows — neither may calibrate. Implementability caveat the lane flagged and I did not close: that Slither exposes `visibility` on the receiver object at effects.py:504, and that immutableReferences survives this pipeline's compile.

verdicts.gap_id: D3 — storage_determined setter identity (flow entry carries no variable / writer_signatures / slot)

Propagating the AST identifier `target_variable` is unimpeachable. `target_writer_scan_complete: true` is not, because of entity keying: effective_functions.deployment_address for ef 423 is 0x8f08b70456eb22f6109f57b8fafe862ed28e6040 (LRTSquaredAdmin is a SECONDARY implementation of that UUPSProxy — contracts.id 461 lists it in secondary_implementations) and for ef 2748 it is 0x89e45081437c959a827d2027135bc201ab33a2c8 (RestakingRewardsRouter 0x6bf6acd4 is its implementation). Slither's `all_state_variables_written()` enumerates the writers inside ONE compiled implementation; at the runtime address the write surface is upgrade-extensible (and for a split proxy, the sibling implementation's writers are outside the unit too). So publishing 'scan complete ⇒ these are the functions, hence the principals, that can redirect this destination' is an unproven exhaustive-negative, on top of the assembly-sstore case the lane already gates.
verdicts.provable_core: Publish `target_variable` (an AST identifier) and `target_writer_signatures` explicitly scoped as the writers WITHIN the analysed compilation unit, with `writer_scan_complete` retained as the assembly/indeterminate gate it already is, PLUS a separate `writer_surface_closed` that is `not_determined` whenever deployment_address is a proxy or the unit is one of several implementations — which is both rows. The derived claim 'redirectable by <principal>' may then be published only as 'redirectable at least by <these writers' principals>', a floor, never as the closed set. Disagreement fold rule (two sites ⇒ target_variables list, no singular key) and absent-vs-[] discipline are correct as proposed. Population 2: mechanical field propagation only, no severity rule.

verdicts.gap_id: D4 — event-cursor coverage: (a) no persisted first_indexed_block, (b) per-variable enrollment hole, (c) silent getLogs truncation
verdicts.reason: All three reproduce. indexed_event_cursors columns are exactly (chain_id, event_address, topic0, last_indexed_block, last_indexed_block_hash, last_run_at, backfill_complete) — no start/first block; 80 rows / 32 distinct addresses / backfill_complete on 80 / last_indexed_block = 25641245 on all 80. The honest half is excellent: (c) is correctly declared NOT provable retrospectively, and the B5.5 / FIELDS §9-limit-4 denylist earned negative is correctly WITHDRAWN rather than softened. The over-claim is the composition of (a)+(b): `absence_coverage: "complete"` is defined as 'every writing topic enrolled and warm', and it is proposed as the gate that LICENSES an earned negative — while (c), in the same report, establishes that page completeness is not_determined for every persisted log row, and (a) establishes the range's lower bound is not persisted at all. A 'complete' verdict assembled from an intent field (first_indexed_block = the seed the enroller INTENDED, not evidence that logs from that height were fetched) plus a truncation-blind fetcher is absence-as-witness without proven coverage of the recording surface — the exact clause §E's last corollary names. That is a fix closing one gap by widening another: it would newly license negatives that its own (c) shows are unproven.
verdicts.provable_core: (a) Add first_indexed_block + first_indexed_block_basis ∈ {creation_block_minus_one, explicit_seed, not_determined}, NULL on all 80 legacy rows meaning 'lower bound unknown', witness-graded only via the two pinned eth_getCode reads (empty at B-1, non-empty at B — demonstrated for 0x3994741a at 20265588/20265589), never from the etherscan_cache alone. (b) Publish `absence_coverage` with a ceiling of `enrollment_complete` — a statement about CURSORS, listing write_surface / enrolled / warm / missing (measured today: toDenyList is 4-of-6 on 0x4de413a2 with AllowTo 0x039bcf51 and DenyTo 0x79fc685a missing, and 0-of-6 on the other three protocol-1 Tellers, i.e. 4 of 24 pairs) — and it must NOT license an earned negative on its own. (c) Move the truncation case into the existing RuntimeError bisect path, persist returned_log_count per window, and only a cursor whose every window carries a sub-cap count may be promoted to `coverage: complete` and license 'no such event exists'. Until then every event-absence negative publishes an unquantified residual; the 26 RoleGranted/RoleRevoked rows on 3 addresses are the only ones upgraded to data-witnessed-complete, and 3-4 addresses may not calibrate an enrollment threshold.

verdicts.gap_id: D5 — router_ops dropped by the claims projection
verdicts.reason: I tried hard to break this and could not. Reproduced: 152 protocol-1 witness flow entries with 0 carrying router_ops, and 41 value_router claims. The fix is a single guarded projection line for a value that is already computed, already pinned in the producer golden, and already consumed IN PROCESS three lines away (services/static/claims/matchers/_facts.py:529, whose docstring states the fail-closed reading of absence). Nothing is inferred: the entries are {selector = keccak4 of the callee's canonical signature, callee = the AST-resolved callee name}, and `_bare_callee_name`'s docstring explains the name is carried precisely because an interface-typed parameter makes the declared signature hash differently. The three-state discipline survives inspection: `if f.get("router_ops")` collapses missing and [] into 'key absent', and absence keeps its existing fail-closed meaning (the router leaf blocks, the mandatory gate falls to not_determined), so no consumer can read [] as 'no router'. No widening: the in-process consumer already reads the producer value, so only a persisted-witness consumer changes, and it changes from not_determined to the same AST fact. One caveat to publish rather than a weakening: `router_ops[].callee` is a bare AST name with no on-chain identity when the selector does not correspond (the interface-typed case), so a consumer must treat it as an intra-unit call identity and never as a resolved on-chain target. And the label-corpus gate is blind unless the pinned witness tuple is extended to the CLAIMS plane — which is why this was invisible.
